⣾⣽⣻⢿⡿⣟⣯⣷mesh-serve: organization, membership, and role CRUD are marked internal, blocking operator mesh exposure FLYBYME/surfdns#65
Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 1 hour ago • 1 comment


   FLYBYME/mesh-operator  declares CRUD contracts for  organization ,         
  membership , and  role  in  mesh.json  for the  people  operator            
  application:                                                                
                                                                              
  •  organization.find ,  get ,  count ,  create                              
  •  membership.find ,  get ,  count ,  create ,  delete                      
  •  role.find ,  get ,  count                                                
                                                                              
  However, in  mesh-serve/src/identity/contracts/identity.contract.ts:55-97 , 
  organizationCrud ,  membershipCrud , and  roleCrud  all define:             
                                                                              
    visibility: {                                                             
        find: 'internal', findOne: 'internal', get: 'internal', resolve:      
  'internal',                                                                 
        count: 'internal', create: 'internal', createMany: 'internal', update:
  'internal',                                                                 
        replace: 'internal', delete: 'internal',                              
    }                                                                         
                                                                              
  Running  mesh-serve client  fails at  descriptor.js:48  because             
  describeExposure  rejects internal contracts. To expose them on operator    
  consoles:                                                                   
                                                                              
  1. Declare  visibility: 'public'  for the permitted actions (e.g.  find ,   
  findOne ,  get ,  count ,  create  for  organization ;  find ,  findOne ,   
  get ,  count ,  create ,  delete  for  membership ;  find ,  findOne ,  get ,
  count  for  role ).                                                         
  2.  membershipCrud  is already  scopedBy: 'organizationId' . For            
  organization  and  role , if global, document/audit per  test/api/visibility.
  test.ts .                                                                   
                                                                              
  Refs FLYBYME/surfdns#63                                                     
                                                                              
  — tony                                                                      


FLYBYME (Owner) • 18m • Newest comment

  Plan for #65:                                                               
                                                                              
  1. Membership CRUD:                                                         
  Expose find, findOne, get, count, create, delete as visibility: 'public'.   
  Existing scopedBy: 'organizationId' handles tenant isolation.               
  2. Role CRUD:                                                               
  Expose find, findOne, get, count as visibility: 'public'. Roles are a global
  platform catalogue containing no tenant data; document this on the contract.
  Add 'role' to GLOBALLY_DELIVERED (events) and DELIBERATELY_GLOBAL           
  (visibility tests).                                                         
  3. Organization CRUD (taking option b):                                     
  Expose find, findOne, get, count, create as visibility: 'public'.           
  Why (b) over (a):                                                           
                                                                              
  • mesh-operator's people app already consumes cx.models('organization') and 
  declares organization.find/get/count/create in mesh.json. If organization.  
  find stays internal, descriptor.js:48 fails mesh-serve client.              
  • Scopes get and count as well, closing cross-tenant probing by ID.         
  Where the join happens:                                                     
  • A companion OrganizationModule (domain: 'organization') registers         
  beforeCrud hooks in the identity module.                                    
  • For find, findOne, and count: reads ctx.meta.user.id, joins against store.
  membershipsOf(userId), and rewrites query.id to { $in: allowedOrgIds }      
  (returning 0 rows if querying another tenant's org).                        
  • For get: checks requested ID is in allowedOrgIds, answering 404 NOT_FOUND 
  if not.                                                                     
  • For create: allows signed-in users to create an organization with ownerId 
  stamped.                                                                    
  • Unauthenticated callers are refused with 401; internal callers without    
  user meta remain unscoped.                                                  
                                                                              
  4. Tests:                                                                   
  Integration tests with two orgs and a single-member user verifying:         
                                                                              
  • Member sees own org's rows.                                               
  • Member sees zero of other org's rows (0 rows on find/count, 404 on get).  
  • Unauthenticated callers rejected (401).                                   
  • Acceptance check: mesh-serve client regenerates cleanly against mesh-     
  operator's mesh.json.                                                       
                                                                              
  — tony

<truncated 24 lines>
+
+1. Read the issue and every comment:
+
+       gh issue view 65 --repo FLYBYME/surfdns --comments
+
+   Note that you wrote it. Read it anyway — what follows disagrees with part
+   of it, and you should see the disagreement in your own words first.
+
+2. Confirm nobody else holds it:
+
+       gh issue view 65 --repo FLYBYME/surfdns --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
+
+   If `bob` or `frank` is there, stop and say so.
+
+3. INVESTIGATE. Read `src/identity/contracts/identity.contract.ts`,
+   `src/api/tools/describe.ts` (this is the ONLY place `visibility` is
+   enforced), `src/api/methods/events.ts`, and `test/api/visibility.test.ts`.
+   Then read a contract that already got this right: `src/cdn/contracts/
+   release.contract.ts` was scoped yesterday, and the breakage it caused is
+   written up in `docs/log/2026-09-07.md`. Read that section before you scope
+   anything.
+
+4. POST YOUR PLAN as an issue comment, signed, before touching a file:
+
+       gh issue comment 65 --repo FLYBYME/surfdns --body "..."
+
+   Keep it short. It is read on a phone.
+
+================================================================================
+WHERE THE ISSUE IS WRONG
+================================================================================
+
+The issue says: declare `visibility: 'public'` for the permitted actions, and
+for `organization` and `role`, "if global, document/audit".
+
+That is not enough, and step 2 is where it goes wrong.
+
+`visibility: 'public'` means MAY BE EXPOSED. It never means unauthenticated —
+that is the gate's job, in the site's grant. So flipping the flag is safe from
+the "anonymous reader" angle and dangerous from a different one:
+
+  * `organizationCrud` has NO `scopedBy`. Make `organization.find` exposable
+    and any signed-in user of any site lists EVERY organization on the
+    platform — every tenant's name, slug and id. That is a tenant leak, and
+    it is exactly the bug `release.find` had (FLYBYME/surfdns#60).
+  * `organization` cannot be fixed with `scopedBy: 'tenantId'`, because an
+    organization IS the tenant. The scope is "organizations I hold a
+    membership in", which is a JOIN, not a field on the row.
+  * `roleCrud` is different and simpler: roles are a global catalogue with no
+    tenant data in them. Reading them at a `user` gate is fine. Say so
+    explicitly rather than by omission.
+  * `membershipCrud` already has `scopedBy: 'organizationId'`, so it is the
+    one the issue describes correctly.
+
+================================================================================
+THE TASK
+================================================================================
+
+Make the `people` application exposable without leaking one tenant to another.
+
+1. `membership` — declare the exposable actions (`find`, `findOne`, `get`,
+   `count`, `create`, `delete`). Its existing `scopedBy: 'organizationId'`
+   does the work. Verify that it does, with a test that a caller scoped to
+   org A gets zero rows for org B — not that it errors, that it gets zero.
+
+2. `role` — declare `find`, `findOne`, `get`, `count` exposable. Global, and
+   deliberately so. Put the reason in a comment on the contract, not only in
+   the PR.
+
+3. `organization` — the real work. A signed-in caller must see the
+   organizations they are a member of, and no others. Decide how, and argue it
+   in your plan comment BEFORE writing code. The options as I see them:
+
+     a. a dedicated tool, `identity.my_organizations`, that resolves
+        memberships then reads organizations. `organization.find` stays
+        internal. Smallest, most obviously correct, and the client asks a
+        question it actually has ("which orgs am I in") instead of filtering.
+     b. a scope resolver on the CRUD itself, so `organization.find` gains a
+        membership-derived filter. More general, and it puts a join in the
+        scoping path, which nothing else does.
+
+   I would take (a). If you take (b), say why and show where the join happens.
+   `organization.create` is a separate question from reading — a signed-in user
+   creating an organization is a real flow, and it does not need a scope.
+
+4. Whatever you choose, `mesh-serve client` must regenerate cleanly —
+   `describeExposure` at `descriptor.js:48` currently throws on these
+   contracts, and "it generates" is the acceptance test the operator console
+   is blocked on.
+
+================================================================================
+THE TEST THAT MATTERS
+================================================================================
+
+Two organizations, a user who is a member of exactly one. Then, for every
+action you declared exposable:
+
+  * the member sees their own org's rows
+  * the member sees ZERO of the other org's rows — not an error, zero
+  * an unauthenticated caller is refused
+
+A test that only proves the happy path proves nothing here. The bug class this
+is preventing is "it worked, and it also returned somebody else's data".
+
+`test/api/visibility.test.ts` is where the existing shape of this lives.
+
+================================================================================
+WHAT NOT TO DO
+================================================================================
+
+  - do NOT change `describeExposure`'s enforcement, or move enforcement to
+    dispatch. That is a real gap (nothing checks `visibility` at dispatch time
+    at all) and it is a SEPARATE issue — open it on FLYBYME/surfdns, signed,
+    and link it. It is not this PR.
+  - do NOT widen scope. A second problem gets a NEW issue, not a bigger PR.
+  - do not delete, skip, or `.only` past a failing test
+  - do not push to master
+
+================================================================================
+FINISHING
+================================================================================
+
+    npm update @flybyme/mesh
+    npm run typecheck
+    npm test
+
+All three, from the worktree root, green. `npm install` alone serves a cached
+git dependency and reports "up to date" — check the installed version actually
+moved. This has cost three separate hours this week.
+
+Then:
+
+    git push origin HEAD:tony/65-people-are-exposable
+    gh pr create --repo FLYBYME/mesh-serve --head tony/65-people-are-exposable \
+      --title "<what changed, not which issue>" --body "<what and why>
+
+    Refs FLYBYME/surfdns#65
+
+    — tony"
+
+Then comment that you are done, signed — link the PR and say what changed
+against the plan you posted, especially anything the plan did not anticipate.
+
+DO NOT MERGE THE PR. The human merges.
+
+================================================================================
+COMMENT AT LEAST TWICE. NEVER WAIT.
+================================================================================
+
+Two comments are the floor: the plan before any code, and the closing report.
+Post more whenever the picture changes — a wrong assumption, a second bug, a
+decision you took. They are the only trace of this run the human ever sees, and
+they read them on a phone.
+
+Nobody replies on GitHub. The human answers through a conversation with bob,
+not in a comment thread, so a run that halts pending a reply halts forever.
+When you would want a decision: say so in a comment with the options and which
+you would pick, CHOOSE ONE, say you are proceeding under that assumption, and
+keep going. Make it easy to undo — a separate commit, or a smaller change.
+
+If you get stuck, finish every part you still can, then post the closing
+comment anyway with the actual error text and what you ruled out. That comment
+is the one required output of a run, more than the PR is: a real diagnosis is
+useful, and silence is indistinguishable from a crash. If you produced no PR,
+say so and say why. A plausible-looking PR that does not work is worse than
+none — say plainly which you have.
